headline: A venture investor spent about $100 on an AI-made sorority hopeful who fooled part of TikTok's Bama Rush audience.
score_reason: Entertaining experiment with useful detection numbers, but the videos date from 8 Aug 2026 and only one outlet's interview reports it.
importance_line: Older viewers were taken in by a synthetic college student while younger ones spotted her at once, and TikTok's own labels caught fewer than half the videos at first; the figures come from the experimenter herself.
summary: Fox News reports that Olivia Moore, an investment partner at venture firm Andreessen Horowitz, built a fictional University of Alabama rush hopeful named Janie with ChatGPT and the MiniMax video model for about $100 in credits and posted her to TikTok from 8 Aug 2026, where her first video drew over 120,000 views. Moore says viewers under 25 spotted the fake quickly while older fans wished her luck, some kept watching after learning the truth, and TikTok at first labelled only 8 of her 20 videos as AI-generated.
notes: Experiment from August 2026 re-reported 3 Oct; score lowered 2 to 1 for staleness.
